title: Chapter 3 Quiz 14
description: Functions that call themselves, with factorial and Fibonacci.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: What is a **recursive** function?
questions.explanation: Recursion is used when the definition of a concept refers to the same concept. Watch out: a loop repeats too, but a recursive function repeats by calling itself.

questions.question: In the factorial function, what is the **base case**?
questions.explanation: The base case stops the recursion. Without it the function would call itself for ever.

questions.question: What is the **recursive case** of the factorial?
questions.explanation: Fact(N) = N × Fact(N-1) when N is not 0. Watch out: the call must use a smaller value to reach the base case.

questions.question: Put the expansion of Fact(3) in order.
questions.explanation: The calls go down to the base case, then the results are multiplied back up.

questions.question: Complete the recursive factorial.
questions.code:
Function Fact(N : integer) Returns integer
Begin
    If N = {{1}} Then
        Fact ← 1
    Else
        Fact ← N * {{2}}
    EndIf
End Function
questions.explanation: The base case is N = 0. The recursive call must use a smaller value: N - 1.

questions.question: Fibonacci: F(0) = 0, F(1) = 1, F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2). Fill in the values.
questions.explanation: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21. Each term is the sum of the two before. Watch out: the sequence starts at F(0) = 0.

questions.question: Why is the simple recursive Fibonacci slow for large n?
options: It never reaches a base case
It only works for even numbers
It uses a loop inside the function
questions.explanation: F(n-1) and F(n-2) both recompute smaller terms again and again. Watch out: it does have base cases, the problem is the repeated work.

questions.question: What does **memoization** do?
options: It turns a function into a procedure
It removes the base case of the function
It sorts the values before the call
It stores computed results for later reuse
questions.explanation: A table remembers results already found, which avoids recalculating.

questions.question: This recursive Fibonacci should return F(n). One line is wrong. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
Function F(n) Returns integer
Begin
    If n <= 1 Then
        F ← n
    Else
        F ← F(n - 1) + F(n)
    EndIf
End Function
questions.explanation: Each term is the sum of the two terms before it. Watch out: F(n) inside F(n) calls itself with the same value and never stops.
